articles.title: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.
The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.”
The supersession, initially imposed for a year, has since been extended annually, first in November 2024, again in November 2025 and now for a further year from November 24, 2026.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

articles.title: OALP deepwater bidding deadline extended again to December 10
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) on Monday extended the deadline for submitting bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the 10th and 11th rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) by 25 days to December 10.

The latest extension marks the seventh for the 10th round, launched in April last year, and the third for the 11th round, which opened in March this year. The deadlines were last extended in September by nearly two months to November 15.
The 10th round offers 25 blocks, including one deepwater and 12 ultra-deepwater blocks, while the 11th round has five blocks on offer, comprising one deepwater and four ultra-deepwater areas.

In August, the Union Cabinet approved an outlay of ₹84,084 crore for the Petroleum Ministry’s National Offshore Exploration Scheme, titled ‘Samudra Manthan’. The corpus, to be utilised until FY31, includes ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.

State-owned explorers ONGC and Oil India have also announced substantial investments in offshore exploration. ONGC plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore by 2030, while Oil India has earmarked ₹15,000 crore over the next three years for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

Brent was down 84 cents, or 0.85%, to $97.48 a barrel by 0138 GMT, while West Texas Intermediate fell 32 cents, or ‌0.35%, to $90.51 a barrel.

The fall reversed minor gains made on Friday’s (November 6, 2026) settlement as the market assessed the ‌possibility of further U.S. strikes on Iran, although Brent fell ‌17% ⁠last week, the steepest weekly drop since the start ⁠of the COVID pandemic and the biggest in absolute terms, according to LSEG data dating back to 1988.
“It depends on whether or not they sign ​a very strong agreement,” Trump ‌told CNN in a phone interview. “The answer is, highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary.”

Mr. Trump had hinted at renewing attacks on Iran after last week’s U.S. midterm elections , but there has ‌been no sign of a large-scale U.S. military operation. ​Iran has said it would respond by striking U.S. and Israeli targets.

Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM ⁠Trade, called Mr. Trump’s comments “more measured” but said “the market is still waiting to see whether the midterms have produced a lasting shift in Trump’s ‌approach to the conflict, or whether this is just another temporary change in tone.”

Oil is headed for a glut again as recovering West Asian oil flows, rising production from other countries and weak demand have pushed global supply above consumption, JPMorgan said in a report on Friday (November 6, 2026), estimating a surplus of 1.1 million barrels ‌per day in September, widening to 1.4 million bpd in October.

Separately the Houthis claimed responsibility for an attack on Saudi Aramco’s offices in the capital Riyadh on Sunday that left windows ​blown out but no reported casualties.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

For a few weeks, Rampur, on the banks of the Sutlej river, comes alive with the fair (November 11-14 this year, with trading grounds open through the month), offering a sensory map of the Himalaya. Colourful textiles, yak wool, pashmina, dry fruits, agricultural produce, Kinnauri apples, indigenous crafts and precious stones fill the marketplace. Among its most captivating sights are the magnificent Chamurthi horses, the hardy “ships of the cold desert”.
Kinnauri weaves on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
At the Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, Shimla district. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
Jewellery on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala

Traders once travelled from Tibet, Nepal, Central Asia and Afghanistan. Tradition traces the fair’s origins to a 17th-century treaty between Raja Kehri Singh of Bushahr and Tibet, establishing it as a meeting point for traders, pilgrims and storytellers along the Silk Route. Though trans-Himalayan trade declined after Tibet’s occupation in 1959, the fair survived on the Buddhist circuit and was accorded international status by the Himachal Pradesh government.

Pratibha Singh, a member of the Rampur Bushahr royal family which founded the fair and continues to honour the tradition, recalls its legacy of pashmina and Kinnauri shawls, some woven over years, alongside trans-Himalayan textiles and local produce. The GI-tagged Kinnauri shawl, with bright geometric motifs, speaks its own language of colour: white for water, yellow for earth, red for fire, green for air, and blue for sky.

On my last visit, a group of elderly women from South India told me they discovered the fair through a fellow traveller whose husband was a biker in the 1990s. A friend from Odisha recalls how in the 90s, his ophthalmologist-father’s eye camps in Rampur led to lifelong friendships and an annual habit of sourcing Kinnauri apples and dry fruits.
Kinnauri apples on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
Traders at Lavi Fair accept payments via UPI now. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala

For Ami Chand Gautam, a Lavi trader since the 1980s, the fair tells a story of changing prices and livelihoods. He remembers when “ chilgoza , the rare pine nut gathered in Kinnaur’s upper reaches, sold for just ₹4-₹5 per kg, almost the price of rice then. Today, it fetches ₹14,000-15,000 per kg,” he says.

fullParagraphs: The White House was briefly placed on lockdown on Monday (November 9, 2026) after a man crashed his car into the sidewalk of a park across from the presidential mansion.
The driver of the vehicle was "quickly placed under arrest" after he "became combative with law enforcement," a U.S. Secret Service spokesperson said.
Video taken by witnesses showed the man struggling with police after being pulled from his car, which crashed into a sign on the sidewalk of Lafayette Park across from the White House.
An explosive ordnance disposal team was called in to "sweep the vehicle as a precaution," the Secret Service spokesperson said in a statement.
Around the same time as the vehicle incident, "a second individual jumped a barricade near the northwest corner of Lafayette Park," the spokesperson said.
"That individual was also quickly placed under arrest," the spokesperson said. "Both incidents are under investigation."
The White House was locked down for around half an hour during the incidents, correspondents said.

articles.title: Comedian Russell Brand sentenced to more than a decade in prison
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: British comedian and Hollywood star Russell Brand was sentenced to ten and a half years in prison for rape and sexual assault by the Southwark Crown Court in London on Monday (November 9, 2026). Brand, 51, was found guilty on Thursday (November 5, 2026) by the court of rape and three counts of sexual assault and not guilty on three other counts. He was charged in relation to a total of seven crimes. His crimes were committed between 2004 and 2009. The court found him guilty of raping a woman in 2009 at his home, after meeting her at a comedy show in the Hammersmith neighbourhood of London. Brand has the possibility of being released in about seven years subject to conditions, the judge said.

“The consequences of what happened have affected almost every aspect of my life. Even now, I continue to experience anxiety, difficulties with trust, reduced confidence and the lasting effects of trauma,” the woman who was raped said on Monday (November 9, 2026) at the sentencing.
One of his victims said she was in “shock and turmoil” and did not “have any respect” for herself as a result of the attack on her. The judge referred to Brand as a “sexual predator”.

Brand had argued during the trial that while his past behaviour had been “wrong”, he had never forced himself on anybody. The actor was formerly a left-wing activist. In the early years of the current decade, he moved to the right, becoming skeptical of vaccines and the origins of COVID-19, building bonds with big names in U.S. President Donald Trump’s Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement, including the President’s son, Donald Trump Jr., tech billionaire Elon Musk , commentators Alex Jones and Tucker Carlson, as well as Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the U.S. Health Secretary. In September, Brand participated in a video call event for the MAHA, Make America Healthy Again, movement, which is headed by Mr. Kennedy Jr. Brand converted to Christianity more recently and was baptized in the Thames in 2024.

articles.title: PM Modi speaks to Ukrainian President Zelenskyy on Kyiv-Moscow conflict, bilateral relations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Modi, on Monday (November 9, 2026), spoke with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict and bilateral relations between Delhi and Kyiv.

According to the PMO, President Zelenskyy shared his perspective on recent developments in the ongoing conflict on the telephone call. PM Modi reaffirmed India’s “human-centric approach” and reiterated India’s consistent position that the conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy. He conveyed India’s readiness to contribute to the peaceful resolution of the conflict.

“We are actively preparing on every item on the agenda for the meeting in Abu Dhabi. Ukraine has always taken a constructive approach, and Russia must show the same readiness to de-escalate,” President Zelenskyy posted on X regarding the talk. “It is important that India identify what steps it can take and what dialogue it can pursue with other leaders to help bring the war to an end.”

Mr. Zelenskyy said that food security could be one of the areas of discussion. “We discussed Russia’s blocking of grain exports via the Black Sea. India is ready to mediate in establishing food corridors, and we are counting on these efforts to continue,” he said.
The two leaders also discussed measures to further strengthen India-Ukraine bilateral cooperation in various sectors.

“Glad to have had a productive telephone conversation with President Zelenskyy. We reviewed our wide-ranging bilateral cooperation and agreed to further strengthen India-Ukraine ties,“ PM Modi said on X. “I thanked President Zelenskyy for sharing his perspectives on the ongoing conflict, its humanitarian aspects and various efforts to restore peace. articles.title: Trump says resumption of war with Iran 'highly unlikely'
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday (November 8, 2026) cast doubt on renewed fighting with Iran, telling CNN that it was "highly unlikely" so long as talks progressed.
In recent weeks, Mr. Trump has threatened to renew strikes with U.S. media reports suggesting that hostilities could resume after the U.S. midterm elections this week.

"The answer is highly unlikely it's going to be necessary... I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don't know how hard I hit them," Mr. Trump said, while warning that any decision to resume hostilities "depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement."
Mr. Trump previously acknowledged that the highly unpopular war with Iran was at least partially responsible for the stinging defeat that his Republican Party suffered in Tuesday's vote.

In the CNN interview on Sunday (November 8, 2026), Mr. Trump once again suggested that the economic pressure Iran is under will force its leaders into accepting a peace deal on the United States' terms.
"They're a failing nation. It just came out, you saw this year, 301 percent inflation," Mr. Trump claimed. "They're withering away financially. We've hit them militarily. We could finish them off."

But earlier on Sunday (November 8, 2026), Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi suggested peace talks had been paused while the political fallout of the Democratic Party's landslide victory was being assessed.

"For the past few days, there has been no more travel (by mediators), and the reason for this is the shock that the election results in the United States have caused to everyone," Mr. Araghchi told state television. "We now have to see how long it will take for them to digest these results, in order to determine how we are going to move forward."

Iran continues to at least partly block traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which has dented oil supplies out of the Gulf. That, in turn, has driven up gasoline prices in the United States, contributing to the unpopularity of the war.

articles.title: Dhaka wants Hasina extradited under prisoner exchange
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Hours after a legal team representing deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina sought a new passport for her, the Government of Bangladesh asserted on Monday (November 9, 2026) that Ms. Hasina can return to Bangladesh through an “acceptable prisoner exchange” programme governed by the India-Bangladesh extradition treaty.
Speaking to the media in Dhaka, the country’s Acting Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir described Ms. Hasina as a “terrorist” who had fled to India after committing crimes.

A source in Dhaka told The Hindu that Ms. Hasina has requested the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through a London-based legal firm, for a new passport and a National Identity Card. The official said the Ministry is verifying the letter and will take a final decision after internal consultations. Ms. Hasina’s passport was revoked soon after she escaped to India in August 2024 after an uprising toppled her government.

“Bangladesh will not issue a passport to any terrorist; there is no provision for such an action. Bangladesh will seek the return of Sheikh Hasina through an acceptable prisoner exchange process,” said Mr. Kabir, in response to questions from journalists regarding the request.

He noted that Ms. Hasina is a convict sentenced to death and has no legal or moral right to obtain a passport. Mr. Kabir said India should hand over the ousted Prime Minister under the extradition treaty. He added that Ms. Hasina and several of her colleagues from the Awami League are responsible for violent crimes and financial fraud, and need to be brought to justice.

The Ministry of External Affairs is yet to respond to Mr. Kabir’s remarks, but a source familiar with the Indian stance on the matter told The Hindu that the Bangladeshi position of not issuing a passport to Ms. Hasina will further complicate the matter, as a passport will be needed if India were to consider her extradition.

The Bangladeshi official, who spoke to The Hindu , said over the phone, “We have received an email from Matrix Chambers, a law firm in London, seeking a new passport for Sheikh Hasina. We are currently examining the contents of the letter and will take an appropriate step after internal consultation.”

However, the Press Secretary of the Bangladesh High Commission, Md. Saidur Rahman, said the Bangladesh authorities are “not sure if the request is genuine”. “There is no way for us to verify whether the request was actually made on behalf of Sheikh Hasina, as the email sent by the law firm did not include any authorisation letter or supporting documents proving that the firm was authorised by her to make such a request,” he said.

articles.title: Twenty-one migrants die trying to reach Greece’s Crete: authorities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Twenty-one people have died over the weekend trying to reach Greece’s island of Crete, a top destination for migrants headed for the European Union from Africa, authorities said on Monday (November 9, 2026).
Eight bodies were found on one boat and 12 on another, while some 40 people were rescued off both, the Greek coast guard said on Monday. Another body was later found on Monday afternoon.
Maritime police launched an emergency rescue late Saturday after a boat issued an alarm signal, with strong winds making sea conditions difficult, the coast guard said.
Around 28 survivors and one body, all Sudanese nationals, were picked up by another boat sailing nearby, then transferred to a police vessel and taken to Crete, authorities had said on Sunday.
Two Sudanese citizens, one of them 16, were arrested after being identified by the survivors as suspected people-smugglers, the authorities said.
During the night from Sunday to Monday, the coast guard found their boat, with seven additional bodies on board, it said.
In a separate incident, 12 bodies were found on a boat south of the island on Monday, while 18 people were rescued, the coast guard said.
In all, the Greek coast guard and the EU’s Frontex border agency rescued a total of 105 on Monday, according to the port authorities.
Crete has become one of the main entry points into the European Union for migrants departing from Libya and attempting the dangerous crossing to Greece.
Many of the attempted crossings turn deadly when the vessels sink or run into trouble.
According to the United Nations refugee agency, more than 37,000 migrants have arrived in Greece in 2026 so far.
Over 22,000 of those people landed on Crete, the country’s largest island.

articles.title: Commercial cultivation within forest land not protected under FRA, 2006: Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court has made it clear that commercial crop cultivation within reserve forest areas is not protected under the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006.

The court has distinguished commercial cultivators and plantation owners from forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers, who have lived in forests for generations and depend on them for livelihood. Their rights are protected under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, commonly known as the FRA.
A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta recorded the court’s view in an order concerning extensive silk cotton cultivation within the reserve forests of the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve.

The court, in its November 6 order, directed the Central Empowered Committee to examine the Tamil Nadu government’s opinion that silk cotton was a ‘minor forest produce’. Presently, 3,637.83 hectares of the 5,072.64 hectares of forest land are under silk cotton cultivation.
However, the Bench made clear its prima facie view against the State’s claim of historical cultivation of silk cotton.

“What emerges from the government affidavits is the promotion and sponsored cultivation of silk cotton as a commercial crop… The concept of planned cultivation of commercial crops is totally contrary to the very concept of a naturally occurring minor forest produce,” the apex court noted.

“We are of the prima facie view that planned or promoted cultivation of a commercial crop inside the forest areas is completely impermissible, as no such right is recognised under the FRA, 2006. The Act recognises the right of forest dwellers to collect, use and dispose of minor forest produce in accordance with Section 3(1)(c). The cultivation of a commercial crop cannot, therefore, be recognised as a forest right so as to justify occupation or continued presence within the forest area,” the Bench said.
ALSO WATCH Will Arunachal Pradesh’s Upper Siang dam protect India against China’s mega-dam? | Insight India
The court did not accept the Tamil Nadu government’s claim that the cultivation of silk cotton justified the presence of the cultivators in the forest area.
“If commercial crops are permitted to be cultivated in the forest areas, the very nature of the forest is bound to change,” Justice Mehta, who authored the order, observed.
The Bench said it was apparent from the government’s own affidavits that large swathes of forest had been destroyed under the garb of silk cotton.cultivation

articles.title: At peak of air pollution on Deepavali night, data goes missing at several govt monitoring stations in Delhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: As Delhiites burst firecrackers well past the 10 p.m. deadline set by the Supreme Court for Deepavali night, air pollution shot up to over 150-200 times World Health Organisation (WHO) limits in parts of the city, but fell through the early morning hours of Monday (November 9, 2026) due to better weather conditions, show official data.

At the peak of pollution , following the bursting of firecrackers on Sunday night (November 8), crucial air quality data were missing from several monitoring stations managed by government authorities. Experts say missing data on peak values of air pollution will artificially show better air quality than the reality.
Though the Supreme Court allowed only green firecrackers during fixed windows on November 7 and 8, traditional firecrackers, which are more polluting, were also available in the markets of Delhi .

As per the Delhi government’s Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) data, the level of PM2.5 (a major pollution) in Patparganj of East Delhi was 2,597 micrograms per cubic metre at 1 a.m. on Monday — about 173.13 times the WHO permissible limit of 15 micrograms per cubic metre for a 24-hour period.

Similarly, the level of PM2.5 in NSUT West Campus was 3,008.4 micrograms per cubic metre at 5 a.m. on Monday (November 9) — about 200.5 times the WHO permissible limit. PM2.5 (Particulate matter 2.5) are fine inhalable particles, which can get into lungs and bloodstream and lead to a range of respiratory and other diseases.

Gufran Beig, chair professor, National Institute of Advanced Studies, said though the air pollution spiked around 12 midnight on Sunday (November 8) to 5 a.m. on Monday (November 9) due to bursting of firecrackers on Deepavali, both wind direction and speed were very favourable for faster dispersion of air pollution.

“The wind direction was earlier north westerly, originating from stubble burning areas in Punjab and Haryana. But around Sunday afternoon, it changed to easterly and south easterly and also picked up speed by Sunday evening. The reversal of wind direction led to almost negligible effect of stubble burning in Delhi,” said Mr. Beig, who is also the founder-director of the Central government’s SAFAR (System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting Research).
Hourly PM2.5 concentrations across Delhi. | Photo Credit: CPCB CAAQMS

The 24-hour average overall Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi stood at 344 (“very poor”) at 4 p.m. on Monday (November 9), lower than 376 (“very poor”) a day earlier, according to the CPCB’s daily bulletin, which is considered the day’s AQI. A higher AQI means worsening of air quality. The overall AQI of Delhi which stood at 370 (very poor) at 9 a.m. on Monday, improved through the day to reach 344 by 4 p.m.

Meanwhile, both the AAP and the Congress attacked the BJP government over the missing data, with the former alleging that it was “data fraud”. Hitting back, Delhi Labour Minister Kapil Mishra alleged there was a “conspiracy” by AAP-governed Punjab to set stubble on fire on Sunday evening.

Every winter, air pollution spikes in Delhi-NCR and many parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains, mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature. Also, pollution from stubble burning during October and November and bursting of firecrackers during the festive season add to existing pollution from vehicles and dust, worsening the air quality.

Meanwhile, Punjab recorded 1,152 stubble burning incidents on Sunday (November 8) — the highest this paddy harvest season, according to the Indian Agricultural Research Institute’s (IARI) daily bulletin. But it dropped to 198 on Monday, taking the total this harvest season to 4,657, the second lowest since 2020 (till November 9), the data show.

articles.title: Chennai sees dozens of cracker-related eye injuries; doctors call for caution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The day may have been wet, but Chennaiites still went all out to bring in light and sparkles on Deepavali day, which fell on Sunday (November 8, 2026). While awareness about safety has increased, ophthalmologists in the city have once again called for caution and reiterated protective measures, as they have received dozens of cases of cracker-related injuries.
The Regional Institute of Ophthalmology and Government Ophthalmic Hospital received around 50 cases, with about 10 cases having to be admitted, a senior official said.

Over the Deepavali weekend, the emergency clinic at Sankara Nethralaya saw 45 cases of firecracker injuries at its main campus. Two underwent wound repair surgery, while two others were scheduled for surgery on Monday, November 9, according to T.S. Surendran, its chairman..

At Dr. Agarwals Eye Hospital, nearly 20 patients came in with cracker-related injuries, said S. Soundari, regional head, clinical services. One of these, she explained, was a very serious case that had been taken up for surgery. Another patient lit a firecracker, but it did not blast. He went near it to take a look, and it blasted in his face, injuring both eyes. The remaining injuries were mostly small, and would be treated medically, she said. Four cases involved children; the rest were adults, mostly in their 30s and 40s.

At Rajan Eye Care, about 15 patients have been seen over the past three days or so, said Mohan Rajan, chairman and medical director of the hospital. One patient had to undergo a surgery, while minor injuries were treated as outpatients.

Doctors have reiterated caution. Dr. Soundari called for wearing protective eye gear while bursting firecrackers, supervising children properly, and importantly, not trying to touch the eye or take objects out by oneself. “Come to a doctor immediately if there is an eye injury,” she stressed. Dr. Rajan noted that bystanders often got hurt and should be careful to maintain an adequate distance..

articles.title: Number of villages without 4G connectivity falls by three-fourths in four years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The number of villages without 4G connectivity has fallen from 45,180 in 2022 to 11,372, about a fourth of the earlier figure, according to data from the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) obtained by The Hindu under the Right to Information Act, 2005. The reduction is partly the result of BSNL’s 4G saturation project. But the figure is beyond the scheme’s initial target of covering 24,680 villages, indicating complementary efforts by private operators.

The reduction is notable because of historical gaps in connectivity between urban and rural India. The country is still far from universal smartphone ownership, even as cities and towns often enjoy extensive high-speed 5G coverage and affordable wired home broadband. The development also comes at a time when additions to wired broadband subscriptions have stagnated for months, making mobile broadband — the primary means of internet access for Indians — all the more important.

fullParagraphs: BJP leader and Delhi Labour Minister Kapil Mishra on Monday (November 9, 2026) alleged that there was a “conspiracy” in AAP-governed Punjab to set stubble on fire in Punjab on Sunday (November 8, 2026) evening, as per official data.

He alleged that 1,200 stubble burning incidents happened in Punjab on Sunday (November 8, 2026) evening, which was 10 times that of previous days. “We got calls from farmers in Punjab that stubble is being set on fire. Someone is coming and setting stubble on fire and running away, when farmers are celebrating Diwali with their families. This is a very serious issue and a conspiracy against Delhi, Punjab, and farmers,” he said.

Earlier in the day, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) attacked the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in Delhi over alleged air quality data “manipulation” by shutting down of air quality monitoring stations.

“The government which shuts down air quality monitoring stations on the night of Diwali, the government that does data fraud, how will you trust such a government?” asked AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj in a video posted on X.

“The government is doing the fraud openly. We had written to the CAQM and CPCB (about the data manipulation). But everyone is silent. This is because everyone is part of this fraud,” Mr. Bharadwaj said.

Last week, the AAP had accused the BJP government of “manipulating” AQI data by spraying water on monitoring stations, and alleged that“fudging” AQI data was not just corruption but life-threatening. The party also wrote to CAQM and CPCB last week, alleging that the Delhi government was manipulating air quality data in the national capital.
When asked about air quality data in Delhi missing in several monitoring stations, Mr. Mishra said that the government will look into the issue within an hour and inform the media about it.

At the peak of pollution following the bursting of firecrackers on Sunday (November 8, 2026) night, data from several monitoring stations operated by the Delhi Government’s Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) were unavailable for hours. This raises the possibility that the actual spike in pollution could have been higher.
Reading from 11:00 a.m. on November 9, 2026, from website of Department of Environment, Government of NCT of Delhi, showing several stations not reporting AQI data.

On Deepavali night, PM2.5 levels in parts of the city soared to 66 times the World Health Organization’s (WHO) recommended 24-hour guideline, before gradually declining in the early hours of Monday (November 9, 2026), according to official data.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

articles.title: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.

articles.title: Trump debacle: On the U.S. midterm election results
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan , making him the first Muslim Senator in history ; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate ; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.
Federal judge orders 14-day delay on any work beginning on Trump’s monumental arch

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

articles.title: Danger in the sewer: On India’s sewer cleaning deaths
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.
• Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

articles.title: Guntur DLSA organises National Legal Services Day
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Every citizen has the right to know their legal rights and access justice, irrespective of where they live, said District Principal Judge and District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) chairman B. Sai Kalyan Chakravarthi.

Speaking at the National Legal Services Day organised by the DLSA in Guntur on Monday (November 9, 2026), he said the Legal Services Authorities Act served as a bridge between the government and beneficiaries by ensuring free legal assistance, promoting legal awareness, and facilitating dispute resolution through Lok Adalats. “Reaching people in remote areas and making them aware of their rights is one of the primary objectives of the authority,” he said.

He emphasised that justice was not limited to punishing offenders, as innocent victims of crimes were also entitled to compensation. Lok Adalats were helping accident victims and their families secure speedy relief in motor vehicle accident cases. They were also facilitating settlements in long-pending civil disputes, he added.

DLSA Secretary Syed Ziyauddin said four National Lok Adalats had settled 90,922 cases, including 5,899 civil and 85,033 criminal cases, involving ₹370.65 crore. Guntur had secured the first position in civil case disposal for the sixth consecutive time by settling 1,784 cases at the March 14, 2026, Lok Adalat.

The authority had conducted 1,120 legal-awareness programmes and resolved 124 cases through the Legal Aid Defence Counsel System. He cited interventions that helped a minor girl resume her education after counselling and provided protection to a woman at a One Stop Centre.

First Additional District Judge V.A.L. Satyavathi, Bar Association president M. Nageswara Rao, and Bar Council members V. Brahma Reddy and Shantha Kumar also spoke. Judges, advocates, para-legal volunteers, and DLSA staff attended the programme.

articles.title: P. T. Usha fails to get elected as SOM; Saina, Anju Bobby George voted in
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Indian Olympic Association President P. T. Usha on Monday (November 9, 2026) failed to get elected, but former shuttler Saina Nehwal made the cut as one of the four women Sportspersons of Merit (SOM) in a field of six candidates following a controversial election.
Legendary long jumper Anju Bobby George, former archer Dola Banerjee and former Indian women’s hockey captain Rani Rampal were also elected as SOM.
Eighty SOM — 40 men and 40 women — form the electoral roll for the election of the four female representatives.

On Saturday (November 7, 2026), Olympic medallists Gagan Narang, Vijender Singh and Yogeshwar Dutt as well as former table tennis player Kamlesh Mehta were elected unopposed as four male SOMs after eight other candidates withdrew their nomination.
Usha can stand for the IOA Executive Council polls to be held on December 5 only if she is nominated to the General Assembly by a National Sports Federation (NSF), which is unlikely.
The track and field legend is not expected to be one of the two representatives from the Athletics Federation of India (AFI).
Under the IOA Constitution, the candidate for the President will have to be an SOM or a member of the General Assembly.
In 2022, Usha was elected unopposed as IOA’s first woman president via the SOM route.
The eight elected SOMs will become members of the IOA General Assembly, making them eligible to vote as well as stand in the December 5 polls of the new Executive Council.
Two SOMs — one man and one woman — will also become members of the IOA Executive Council.

Controversy struck the IOA SOM election when Usha lodged a complaint with Electoral Officer Sanjay Kumar Srivasatava, alleging that former archer Dola Banerjee violated the Model Code of Conduct by circulating a WhatsApp message soliciting votes.

In her complaint, Usha objected to a WhatsApp message circulated through an account bearing Banerjee’s name, seeking support for the ‘New Bharat Panel’ and specifically asking voters to elect four named candidates, along with their ballot serial numbers and roll numbers.

fullParagraphs: Two minor boys were murdered at Samayapuram near Tiruchi in the late night hours on Sunday (November 8). The killers are yet to be identified.

Police identified the victims as S. Rahul, 17, and R. Vishal, 17, — both of Inam Samayapuram village in Manachanallur taluk. The victims were relatives and engaged in garland making work at Samayapuram.

The motive behind the double murder and details of those involved in the killings are under investigation as Samayapuram police registered a murder case.

Meanwhile, the police said the five special teams constituted to probe the case had identified six suspects in the case. The suspected persons were being pursued by the teams. The exact motive behind the crime could be established only after the accused were apprehended. The sources said the victims and the suspected persons were friends.

articles.title: Belagavi Police arrest woman, six accused for murdering her son
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Belagavi Police have arrested seven people, including a 44-year-old woman, on the charge of killing the woman’s 24-year-old son.
Meena Narayana, a resident of R.T. Nagar in Bengaluru, her 34-year-old friend Rakesh Parashurama Jamuni of Ichalkaranji in Maharashtra and his five associates have been arrested.
The names of four of Jamuni’s associates were given as Sachin Kamble, Manoj Kamble, Tammanna Kamble and Eknath Kamble. The other accused is a child in conflict with law.
The seven accused eliminated Meena’s son Vijaya Narayana after he objected to his widowed mother’s relationship with Jamuni, the police said.
The body was found in a drain on Kolhapur Road last week.
Investigators found strangulation marks on Vijaya Narayana’s neck and registered a murder case.
Meena visited the police station and identified the body found in the drain as that of her son Vijaya Narayana on Wednesday last.
The accused is said to have drugged the victim with a drink and killed him in Belagavi on November 1. They dumped the body in the drain and fled, the police said.

articles.title: KMC Commissioner directs officials to identify dumping spots, boost awareness on waste disposal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kurnool Municipal Corporation (KMC) Commissioner Challa Obulesu has directed officials to identify roads, vacant plots, and other public spaces where garbage is being dumped and to create awareness among the residents to discourage indiscriminate dumping. The KMC Commissioner also instructed officials to ensure public cooperation with the door-to-door waste collection system.

Mr. Obulesu inspected the sanitation operations in Gibson Colony, Birla Gate, Krishna Nagar, and Chennamma Circle on Monday. Subsequently, at the Kalluru ward office, he examined the equipment recently procured for water supply and repair works.

During an inspection of the Anna Canteen at the government hospital, the sanitation supervisory staff brought to the Commissioner’s attention the challenges they faced regarding waste collection. Responding immediately, the Commissioner consulted with the sanitation staff and issued orders to ensure that waste was collected from the hospital twice daily.
He emphasised that waste collection must continue without interruption, even on public holidays.

articles.title: Sabarimala ghee supply in a bind; TDB opens talks with Milma
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: With the Mandala-Makaravilakku season in Sabarimala barely a week away, the Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) is turning to Milma once again to plug the gap in ghee supply after two rounds of tendering failed to find eligible bidders.

The board had invited bids for 50,000 litres of ghee but failed to find eligible suppliers. Though Milma did not participate in the tender, the TDB has been holding discussions with office-bearers of the Milma Thiruvananthapuram Regional Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union.
TDB president K. Jayakumar said the board was yet to take a final call on procuring ghee from Milma for Aravana production and would seek legal advice before deciding on the matter.

According to him, the anticipated shortfall at the beginning of the season was only around 10,000 litres and there was no immediate cause for concern over availability. Ghee supplies were expected to increase once the temple opens on November 16, though the shortfall could affect production until then. Preparations for Aravana production are progressing, with the board currently holding a stock of 30 lakh tins. Arrangements are being finalised to produce 3.5 lakh tins daily.
“We are planning to produce another 30 lakh tins in the coming days. Appam production will also begin in a time-bound manner,” Mr. Jayakumar said.

Milma’s possible return as a supplier comes amid an ongoing Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) probe into the supply of spurious ghee to the Sannidhanam in its name last season. The investigation found that the contractor entrusted with transporting the ghee had diverted around 11,000 kg of Milma ghee meant for Sabarimala and replaced it with a cheaper product.

Meanwhile, the deadline for completing construction and other preparatory works, including maintenance, ahead of the season expires on Tuesday. Despite the TDB’s claims that preparations are complete, sources said several works at the Sannidhanam and Nilackal, including road reconstruction, remain unfinished and could take another week to complete.

articles.title: OALP deepwater bidding deadline extended again to December 10

fullParagraphs: The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) on Monday extended the deadline for submitting bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the 10th and 11th rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) by 25 days to December 10.

The latest extension marks the seventh for the 10th round, launched in April last year, and the third for the 11th round, which opened in March this year. The deadlines were last extended in September by nearly two months to November 15.
The 10th round offers 25 blocks, including one deepwater and 12 ultra-deepwater blocks, while the 11th round has five blocks on offer, comprising one deepwater and four ultra-deepwater areas.

In August, the Union Cabinet approved an outlay of ₹84,084 crore for the Petroleum Ministry’s National Offshore Exploration Scheme, titled ‘Samudra Manthan’. The corpus, to be utilised until FY31, includes ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.

State-owned explorers ONGC and Oil India have also announced substantial investments in offshore exploration. ONGC plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore by 2030, while Oil India has earmarked ₹15,000 crore over the next three years for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

For a few weeks, Rampur, on the banks of the Sutlej river, comes alive with the fair (November 11-14 this year, with trading grounds open through the month), offering a sensory map of the Himalaya. Colourful textiles, yak wool, pashmina, dry fruits, agricultural produce, Kinnauri apples, indigenous crafts and precious stones fill the marketplace. Among its most captivating sights are the magnificent Chamurthi horses, the hardy “ships of the cold desert”.
Kinnauri weaves on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
At the Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, Shimla district. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
Jewellery on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala

Traders once travelled from Tibet, Nepal, Central Asia and Afghanistan. Tradition traces the fair’s origins to a 17th-century treaty between Raja Kehri Singh of Bushahr and Tibet, establishing it as a meeting point for traders, pilgrims and storytellers along the Silk Route. Though trans-Himalayan trade declined after Tibet’s occupation in 1959, the fair survived on the Buddhist circuit and was accorded international status by the Himachal Pradesh government.

Pratibha Singh, a member of the Rampur Bushahr royal family which founded the fair and continues to honour the tradition, recalls its legacy of pashmina and Kinnauri shawls, some woven over years, alongside trans-Himalayan textiles and local produce. The GI-tagged Kinnauri shawl, with bright geometric motifs, speaks its own language of colour: white for water, yellow for earth, red for fire, green for air, and blue for sky.

On my last visit, a group of elderly women from South India told me they discovered the fair through a fellow traveller whose husband was a biker in the 1990s. A friend from Odisha recalls how in the 90s, his ophthalmologist-father’s eye camps in Rampur led to lifelong friendships and an annual habit of sourcing Kinnauri apples and dry fruits.
Kinnauri apples on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
Traders at Lavi Fair accept payments via UPI now. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala

For Ami Chand Gautam, a Lavi trader since the 1980s, the fair tells a story of changing prices and livelihoods. He remembers when “ chilgoza , the rare pine nut gathered in Kinnaur’s upper reaches, sold for just ₹4-₹5 per kg, almost the price of rice then. Today, it fetches ₹14,000-15,000 per kg,” he says.

articles.title: Rubio says Trump's war against Iran not 'necessarily popular' but needed to stop a nuclear threat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Sunday (November 7, 2026) that President Donald Trump launched the war against Iran, even if it was not “necessarily popular”, to safeguard the world from the country's nuclear ambitions.

He would not comment directly about the Republican wipeout in Tuesday's (November 3) elections, which delivered a resounding rebuke to Mr. Trump. The unpopularity of the Iran war and its impact on gasoline prices and other parts of the economy helped Democrats seize control of Congress.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Marco Rubio: Iran can never be allowed to become a nuclear weapons power

Asked about Vice-President J.D. Vance's social media post last week that largely blamed the war for the Republican losses, Mr. Rubio told reporters that Mr. Trump “identified a very real threat” in Iran and worked to stop the Islamic Republic from pursuing a nuclear weapon.
Trump to meet Iran war mediator Qatar, no imminent deal seen to end war

“He addressed it even though oftentimes the right thing to do for the country — confronting difficult challenges for the security of our country — doing it isn't necessarily popular, but necessary,” Mr. Rubio said in Florida before heading to a Group of 7 Foreign Ministers meeting in Paris.

America's top diplomat offered a robust defence of the more than eight-month-old war even as voters blamed Mr. Trump's policies for the hit to their pocketbooks, including higher energy prices that stemmed from disruptions to shipments in the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway where one-fifth of the world's oil transited before the war.

Mr. Rubio's comments also put him at odds with Mr. Vance amid speculation of both of their 2028 presidential ambitions. Mr. Trump told reporters on Sunday (November 7) that Mr. Vance was right — other than that his Vice-President should have also insisted it was the correct choice to go to war.
“I can tell you, this historically — for history — will go down as one of the best things we ever did," Mr. Trump said. "Because if they ever had a nuclear weapon, they would blow up the world."

Iran has long maintained that its nuclear programme is peaceful. According to the International Atomic Energy Agency, Iran has 440.9 kg of uranium that is enriched up to 60% purity, a short, technical step from weapons-grade levels of 90%.
With no clear administration strategy to wind down the conflict and West Asia on edge over the possibility of a return to major hostilities, mediators are trying to revive talks between the sides.
Mr. Rubio said, “I wouldn't say we're at the verge of a breakthrough.”

Beijing said on Monday (November 9, 2026) it was “in communication with relevant parties” over the meeting, not ruling out the possibility as leaders gather for the APEC summit in southern China on November 18 and 19.

Mr. Trump on Sunday (November 8, 2026) indicated to reporters that a deal on the Russia-Ukraine war, the Iran issue and nuclear arms control would be on the agenda. “One of the meetings will be with President Putin and President Xi, and that’ll be interesting. We’re talking ​a lot of things, including denuclearisation, but we’ll ​be talking a lot of things. We’re trying to end the ‌war ⁠in Iran,” Mr. Trump was quoted as saying.

Asked about his remarks, China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun on Monday (November 9, 2026) did not rule out the prospect of a meeting, saying that China was in communication with relevant parties regarding the meeting between the Chinese, Russian and U.S. Presidents.

Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi will meet bilaterally next week for the third time this year, following the U.S. President’s visit to Beijing in May and the Chinese President travelling to Washington in September . They will meet once again at the end of the year at the G20 in Miami, marking an unusual four meetings in a year.

Both countries have sought to inject more stability in relations and pursue what they call “a constructive relationship of strategic stability”, even as they have exchanged blows on issues including trade tariffs, restrictions on semiconductors, rare earths and Taiwan.

Chinese analysts have sought to play down the significance of a possible trilateral summit, just as they also played down Mr. Trump’s remarks in Beijing earlier this year of a “G2”. Russia was “most enthusiastic” among the three, Su Liuqiang, a scholar at the Centre for American Studies at the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies, said in an interview with state media, adding that an informal exchange was likelier than a more structured, formal trilateral summit.

“On the one hand, there is substantial political resistance in the U.S. Anti-Russia sentiment remains strong in both the U.S. and among its European allies, with opposition to negotiating with Moscow while bypassing Ukraine and Europe. On the other hand, the three countries have differing priorities. Russia’s core concern is negotiations on a ceasefire in Ukraine, the U.S. is interested in the Russia-Ukraine conflict and non-proliferation, China supports peace talks but must also balance its relations with the U.S., Russia, Europe and Ukraine. In this context, a low-profile trilateral meeting is the more realistic option,” he said, adding that practical outcomes could emphasise stabilising global energy supplies.

While China preferred “multilateralism” over ideas such as the G2 or a U.S.-China-Russia triumvirate, Mr. Su said a meeting would still be significant in suggesting that while structural competition between big powers would still continue to define global geopolitics, there was increasing interest in “managing that competition and preventing it from escalating or spinning out of control”.

articles.title: Six dead in blast at steel factory near Turkiye’s Izmir: officials
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Six people were killed and around a dozen injured on Monday (November 9, 2026) when an explosion ripped through an iron and steel factory near Turkiye western resort city of Izmir, the governor's office said.

The governor's office initially gave a toll of three dead, 14 injured and 10 trapped under the rubble, but gave an update saying one of the injured had died along with two of those pulled from the rubble, raising the toll to six.
The massive blast took place around midday (0900 GMT) at the Habas Demir Celik factory in Aliaga, about 60 kilometres (37 miles) north of Izmir, with officials saying it sparked a fire at the plant.
The DHA news agency said initial findings suggested the blast occurred when an overhead crane collapsed into a large industrial furnace used during the liquid steel casting process.
Izmir Mayor Cemil Tugay said rescue teams were "continuing their work to remove the collapsed platform" and that those affected were factory workers.

"Unfortunately, we have received preliminary information indicating a large number of deaths and injuries among people working at the factory. The exact number will become clear once the wreckage has been removed," he said in a post on X shortly before the toll was updated to six dead.

articles.title: Trump to meet Iran war mediator Qatar, no imminent deal seen to end war
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump will meet ‌the Prime Minister of key mediator Qatar on Monday (November 9, 2026) as efforts to end the ​Iran war ramp up following last week's midterm elections, though senior U.S. and Gulf ⁠officials cast doubt on the chances of an imminent deal.

With no victory in sight more than eight months into the conflict he launched alongside Israel on February 28, Mr. Trump has played down the likelihood of major warfare restarting soon, but remains ‌unwilling to accept an existing Iranian truce plan.

Mutual attacks continue, with the U.S. striking Iran's Qeshm island overnight, according to Iranian state media, and Iran attacking tankers in the Gulf and ‌Strait of Hormuz this month while its Yemeni Houthi allies have hit Saudi Arabia.

Sheikh Mohammed ‌bin ⁠Abdulrahman Al-Thani, who is both Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Qatar, will meet Mr. ⁠Trump and Vice President J. D. Vance in Washington later on Monday (November 9, 2026) after having visited Tehran last week.

Iran's proposal to end the war involves an end to the U.S. blockade of its ports, the lifting of some sanctions, and a halt to bombing in return for ​Tehran stopping its own blockade of the Strait ‌of Hormuz, with talks on its nuclear programme and other sanctions to follow.

The U.S. has repeatedly rejected that plan, which Iran has said could be condensed to a two-day timeframe, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Sunday (November 8, 2026) describing Tehran's conditions as "outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic".
Iran's Foreign Ministry ‌spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei defended the plan on Monday (November 9, 2026) as the most reasonable offer on the table.

Senior ​U.S. Republicans including Mr. Vance have blamed their party's dire showing in last week's elections on the Iran war, but despite growing domestic political pressure to end the conflict, Mr. Rubio said ⁠he did not believe a diplomatic breakthrough was imminent.
A senior United Arab Emirates official, Anwar Gargash, echoed that view on Monday (November 9, 2026), saying a comprehensive political settlement between the U.S. and Iran appeared difficult.
"We should... prepare for a ‌long period of uncertainty in which neither a decisive resolution nor stable regional order can be taken for granted," he said.

Mr. Vance, who led the negotiations for a short-lived truce in June, will also meet Mr. Al-Thani, whose country has been a prime mediator since early in the war, conveying messages between the sides and proposing ways to bridge their differences.

Sunday (November 8, 2026) night's strikes on Qeshm island did not impact vital infrastructure or services, a provincial official told Iran's semi-official Fars news agency on Monday (November 9, 2026). The U.S. has not commented on the Iranian ‌media reports.

articles.title: Pakistani TV anchorperson shot dead at home in Rawalpindi; husband held
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A Pakistani anchorperson was shot dead at her home in Rawalpindi, with police taking her husband into custody and seizing the suspected weapon.

Rabia Ahsan, who worked as an anchor and programme host with a local private TV channel, was found dead at her home in the Gulshanabad area of the city on Sunday (November 8, 2026), the Dawn newspaper reported.
City Police Officer (CPO) Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera said Ahsan's husband had been taken into custody and the suspected weapon seized. An investigation has been launched, he added.
Mr. Sukhera, along with the senior superintendent of police (SSP) operations and the SSP investigations, visited the crime scene with a team of forensic experts.
According to the CPO, a male domestic worker at the house told police that the victim's husband had claimed that the gunshot was fired accidentally.
Mr. Sukhera said teams from the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) were collecting evidence from the scene, while the body was being taken to a hospital for postmortem examination.
A case was being registered and an investigation would be conducted on merit, he said.
Meanwhile, First Lady Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari expressed deep sadness over the killing and strongly condemned the violence.
She called for a thorough, impartial and transparent investigation to establish the facts and ensure that those responsible were held accountable, a statement issued by the Presidency said.
Ms. Bhutto-Zardari also expressed concern over what she described as a “disturbing pattern of killing of another professional woman in the same metropolitan area”.

She recalled the murder of Hina Javed, a 45-year-old digital media executive who was found dead at her Rawalpindi residence in August with signs of torture, and noted that the outcome of the investigation into the case was still awaited.
